name: agilex7_wideband_control_plane
description: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the register/control plane. Hand edited; nothing
generates this file. scripts/gen_regmap.py reads it and emits the SystemVerilog
package, the C++ harness header, the human table and the machine-readable map.
Editing any generated artefact by hand is a defect: `make regmap-check` (also run
by `make lint` and `make sim-tiny`) regenerates and fails on any difference.
JSON, not YAML: the repository ships no YAML parser and requirements.txt carries
only numpy, so a YAML source of truth would add a dependency to a clean checkout
for no expressive gain. JSON has no comments, so every rationale that would have
been a comment is a `description` field instead - which is strictly better, because
descriptions flow into docs/regmap.md and into the generated SystemVerilog header
comments rather than dying in the source file.
notes: Address space: byte addressed, 16 bits, one 4 KiB window per block.
Registers are 32 bits and word aligned; address[1:0] != 0 is an error response.
Within a block, register offsets must be dense from 0 (offset == index * 4). The
generator enforces this: the RTL decode is an index compare, not a CAM.
A read or write to an address inside a block window but beyond that block's last
register returns error=1, as does any address outside every implemented window.
Field access types:
RO   constant read-only. The field's `reset` IS its value; writes are refused.
ROHW read-only, driven by hardware (status, build parameters, counters).
RW   read-write storage.
W1C  sticky bit, set by hardware, cleared by writing 1. Writing 0 does nothing.
RWP  RW-pulse: a written 1 emits a one-cycle pulse and the bit reads back 0.
A register whose fields are all RO or ROHW is not writable at all: a write to it
completes with error=1 and no side effect. A register with a mix of writable and
non-writable fields accepts the write and silently ignores the non-writable bits.
Computed reset tokens (resolved by scripts/gen_regmap.py, never by hand):
$N_BLOCKS      number of declared blocks, implemented and planned
$N_REGS_TOTAL  number of implemented registers across all blocks
$BLOCK_MASK    bit i set when declared block i is implemented
$DATA_W        register data width in bits
$ADDR_W        register address width in bits
$VERSION_MAJOR, $VERSION_MINOR, $VERSION_PATCH  from regmap_version below

regmap_version.description: Bump on any change to this file. major: incompatible layout change; minor: registers or fields added; patch: documentation only.

blocks.name: id
blocks.description: Fixed identification of the control plane itself. Every field is a constant folded in at elaboration, so a live design can be identified without any prior knowledge of what was built.

registers.name: MAGIC
registers.description: Constant marker. Reading 0x52414441 ('RADA') at block base proves a control plane is present and the address decode is alive.

registers.name: VERSION
registers.description: Register-map version, from regmap_version in the source of truth. Static build data, deliberately not a git describe: the same source tree must produce the same register contents on any machine, and a VCS-derived value would make the generated artefacts depend on checkout state.

registers.name: GEOMETRY
registers.description: Shape of the register plane, so a discovery walk needs no compiled-in constants.

registers.name: CAPABILITY
registers.description: One bit per declared block, set when that block is implemented in this build. Bit i is block i in declaration order; a planned block reads 0 and its window returns error.

blocks.name: build_params
blocks.description: Read-only mirror of the elaboration parameters. Every value is driven from config_pkg, which scripts/build_verilator.py generates from config/<name>.json (SPEC 11), so this block reports what was actually elaborated rather than what a header claims.

registers.name: N_ANTENNAS
registers.description: SPEC 11 sized parameter.

registers.name: SAMPLES_PER_CYCLE
registers.description: SPEC 11 sized parameter.

registers.name: FFT_SIZE
registers.description: SPEC 11 sized parameter.

registers.name: PFB_TAPS
registers.description: SPEC 11 sized parameter.

registers.name: N_BEAMS
registers.description: SPEC 11 sized parameter.

registers.name: HISTORY_FRAMES
registers.description: SPEC 11 sized parameter.

registers.name: PACKET_W
registers.description: SPEC 11 sized parameter.

registers.name: SAMPLE_W
registers.description: SPEC 3 invariant parameter.

registers.name: COEFF_W
registers.description: SPEC 3 invariant parameter.

registers.name: POWER_W
registers.description: SPEC 3 invariant parameter.

registers.name: N_VIRTUAL_CHANS
registers.description: SPEC 3 invariant parameter.

registers.name: PARAM_CHECKSUM
registers.description: FNV-1a 32 over the eleven parameter words above, in offset order, little-endian bytes. Computed in RTL from config_pkg and independently in the C++ harness from config_sim.h: a mismatch means the RTL and the harness were elaborated from different configurations, which is otherwise a silent and very expensive failure.

blocks.name: ctrl
blocks.description: Per-block enable and soft-reset stubs. The bit assignment is fixed now so that each kernel issue wires its own enable and reset without renumbering anything; a bit whose consumer has not landed drives an output of control_top and nothing else.

registers.name: BLOCK_ENABLE
registers.description: Per-block enable. Reset value enables every block, so a build with no software present still runs.

registers.name: BLOCK_RESET
registers.description: Per-block soft reset request. Writing 1 emits a one-cycle pulse in the cfg_clk domain; the bit always reads 0. Crossing the pulse into each block's own domain is issue #6 work and is deliberately not done here.

fields.name: PFB
fields.description: Pulse a soft reset at the PFB.

fields.name: FFT
fields.description: Pulse a soft reset at the FFT.

fields.name: BEAMFORMER
fields.description: Pulse a soft reset at the beamformer.

fields.name: COVARIANCE
fields.description: Pulse a soft reset at the covariance engine.

fields.name: CFAR
fields.description: Pulse a soft reset at the CFAR detector.

fields.name: PACKET
fields.description: Pulse a soft reset at the packet fabric.

fields.name: MEMORY
fields.description: Pulse a soft reset at the history memory.

fields.name: TELEMETRY
fields.description: Pulse a soft reset at the telemetry block.

registers.name: GLOBAL_CTRL
registers.description: Datapath-wide control. GLOBAL_ENABLE gates every block regardless of BLOCK_ENABLE.

registers.name: CTRL_STATUS
registers.description: Hardware-driven status. ENABLED_COUNT is computed in the block from the live BLOCK_ENABLE value, so it exercises a real hardware read path rather than mirroring storage.

fields.name: ALIVE
fields.description: Tied high by the block; reads 1 whenever the control plane is out of reset.

blocks.name: fault
blocks.description: Fault injection (SPEC 24). Injection is two-step on purpose: a persistent arming mask plus a one-shot trigger. A single stray write can therefore never inject a fault, and the arming state is visible in a register dump taken after the fact.

registers.name: FAULT_ENABLE
registers.description: Arming mask. A trigger bit has no effect unless the matching enable bit is set.

fields.name: PACKET_DROP
fields.description: Drop a packet in the packet fabric.

registers.name: FAULT_INJECT
registers.description: One-shot triggers, same bit assignment as FAULT_ENABLE. Writing 1 to an armed bit emits a one-cycle pulse and sets the matching FAULT_STATUS bit. Always reads 0.

registers.name: FAULT_STATUS
registers.description: Sticky record of faults actually injected, set by hardware and cleared by writing 1. A hardware set in the same cycle as a software clear wins, so an event is never lost to a racing clear.

registers.name: FAULT_COUNT
registers.description: Free-running count of injected fault pulses (one per armed bit per trigger). Saturating, not wrapping, so a dump taken long after the event still reports 'many' rather than an ambiguous small number.

blocks.name: scratch
blocks.description: Software scratch registers with no hardware effect. They exist to test the fabric itself: four distinct reset values prove per-register reset defaults, and SCRATCH3 mixes a writable half with a read-only half so that partial writability is covered by construction rather than by a future block happening to need it. The snapshot and debug-control group proper lands with issue #19 in the debug window.

registers.name: SCRATCH0
registers.description: Scratch, reset all zeros.

registers.name: SCRATCH1
registers.description: Scratch, reset all ones.

registers.name: SCRATCH2
registers.description: Scratch, alternating reset.

registers.name: SCRATCH3
registers.description: Half writable, half constant. A write updates RW_LOW and leaves RO_HIGH untouched, and the transaction succeeds (error=0) because the register is partially writable.

fields.name: RO_HIGH
fields.description: Constant half; writes are ignored, not refused.

blocks.name: coeff
blocks.description: PLANNED. Coefficient and beam-weight programming with double buffering and an active-bank select. Declared here so the window is reserved and the address space cannot be reassigned by a later issue; unimplemented until its owning issues land, and every access to this window returns error=1 today.

blocks.name: cfar
blocks.description: PLANNED. CFAR guard/training geometry and threshold scaling, plus coherent and non-coherent integration settings.

blocks.name: counters
blocks.description: PLANNED. Performance and health telemetry. The counters themselves are issue #8; this window is where they are read from. Counters live in the telemetry clock domain, so this block will be the first consumer of the issue #6 CDC primitives on the register path.

blocks.name: debug
blocks.description: PLANNED. Snapshot capture, trigger configuration and debug readback.
